name: openserp-repeatable-fingerprint-regression-3ca1
instr:
openserp cannot persist known-good fingerprint evidence or compare it with later local runs. Add durable, repeatable baselines and extend the debug fingerprint endpoint with capture and compare operations, without changing ordinary reports. Results must be deterministic and versioned, preserving detector-owned identity across unlike extractors.

Every standard detector exposes stable, ordered `SignalDefinition` values using detector-scoped `SignalKey` keys through `Detector.Signals`; reject duplicates. Custom detectors without definitions remain report-only. `NewBaseline` accepts only complete successful reports. `Baseline`, `BaselineDetector`, and `BaselineSignal` preserve all evidence through `BaselineStore`. Unsupported versions return a typed compatibility error without a partial value.

Baselines use format version 1. `Compare` returns an ordered `Comparison` of `SignalChange` values. Classify each `ChangeKind` as `ChangeAdded` (`"added"`), `ChangeRemoved` (`"removed"`), `ChangeChanged` (`"changed"`), `ChangeUnchanged` (`"unchanged"`), or `ChangeUnavailable` (`"unavailable"`). `ComparisonPolicy` applies `NumericAbsoluteTolerance` only to eligible numeric evidence; boolean verdicts and severity remain exact.

Baseline replacement must be atomic and validate existing content. Cancellation, extraction failure, unsupported detectors, malformed data, or write failure must preserve the prior baseline and leave no temporary artifact.

Support `FingerprintOperation` values `Fing
